textures.use: Projected complete standing pier figures, arched window surrounds, two inscription fields, upper ornament and carved arch fields. The window aperture and surrounding photograph share the same traced outline.

sampling.method: projective UV selection from full source image
sampling.geometryPlacement: scripts/church/dubrovitsy-interior.py: _di_source_aperture and _di_window_bay register the physical tower aperture to the source; _di_cartouche_bay, _di_cartouche_bay_right and _di_carved_frieze supply other repeated fields. textures.title: Crucifixion relief and upper iconostasis
textures.author: Goussew
textures.angle: Centered view toward east Crucifixion relief over the iconostasis; high-resolution 2023 image includes only the top of the gilded screen. · 2023-06-18
textures.modifications: No raster alteration. Full source image retained. Model meshes select and rectify image regions with UV coordinates, with model lighting and material response applied at render time. Resulting adaptations retain CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution.
textures.limitations: The original photograph crops out the lower iconostasis and the chandelier obscures parts of the center. It is not a complete screen texture. Curved projection, source contours, shallow depth and repeated leaf/ribbon placements are inferred. The retained source bytes do not guarantee distortion-free or visually accepted geometry.
textures.use: Projected crossing lunettes, terminal vault ornament, upper icon painting fields, bounded acanthus screen ornament and the narrow running acanthus ribbon on the modeled tier cornices. Also a reference for the east Crucifixion arrangement; the large east Crucifixion texture itself remains the separately credited recovered legacy selection.

sampling.method: projective UV selection from full source image
sampling.geometryPlacement: scripts/church/dubrovitsy-interior.py: bounded crossing lunettes, terminal vault projection and _di_tier_cornice; scripts/church/dubrovitsy-iconostasis.py: upper paintings and bounded leaf ornament. Dimensions and repeat placement remain photographic estimates.

regions.label: Running acanthus ribbon below the Resurrection, right of the suspension chain
regions.geometryPlacement: scripts/church/dubrovitsy-interior.py: _di_cornice_ribbon and _di_tier_cornice. Two complete repeats per octagonal facet on the two wider tier returns; photographic strip over a modeled ogee section. Physical scale and profile depth are inferred.

textures.title: Crucifixion and upper octagon in daylight
textures.angle: Looking up past the upper iconostasis toward the Crucifixion, sculpted octagon, and enclosed blue vault · 10 May 2019
textures.use: Three distinct projective UV selections supply narrative relief on the three solid eastern octagon faces. Conservative whole-group outer envelopes remove surrounding architectural photo margins and taper into modeled blue masonry. The full image also documents the iconostasis crest, Crucifixion and upper vault.
textures.limitations: Oblique perspective, captured daylight and local source resolution constrain usable detail. The outer envelopes are conservative hand-authored approximations, not exact sculptural segmentation; some extremities or architectural context may be imperfectly retained. Interior blue spaces are kept rather than isolating white pixels. Narrative dimensions, depth and placement remain photographic estimates.

materialSources.title: White Plaster 02 · fine plaster finish source
materialSources.author: Rob Tuytel
materialSources.angle: Generic fine plaster normal and roughness supplied by Poly Haven; not a photograph of Dubrovitsy
materialSources.use: Subtle mineral normal and roughness variation on the modeled blue limewash and chalk stucco. Existing authored blue and chalk base colors remain unchanged. Only the OpenGL normal and packed ARM image are used; diffuse and standalone roughness originals are retained but unused.
materialSources.modifications: All four retained source JPEGs are unchanged. Normal strength and roughness factors are authored material settings, not raster edits. Standard glTF exports the original normal and ARM JPEG bytes; the ARM blue channel has a zero metallic factor and its red AO channel is unused.
materialSources.limitations: This generic material is not a scan, photograph or measured survey of Dubrovitsy plaster. The one-metre repeat and subtle material response are interpretive; per-face metric UV islands can introduce fine orientation seams.
